examples: Financially, the move to Texas made a lot of sense.
The plan looks good financially, but it will take years.
Financially, we're in much better shape than last year.
My parents still support me financially.
She wants to be financially independent by thirty.
A lot of families are struggling financially right now.

senses.head: From the point of view of money; when money is considered
body: (с финансовой точки зрения, в финансовом плане)
examples: Financially, the move to Texas made a lot of sense.
The plan looks good financially, but it will take years.
Financially, we're in much better shape than last year.

senses.head: In a way that concerns money — having it, earning it, or giving it
examples: My parents still support me financially.
She wants to be financially independent by thirty.
A lot of families are struggling financially right now.

entries.type: viewpoint; also manner — in terms of money
entries.position: any position — front with a comma as a viewpoint (Financially, it works); before an adjective (financially stable); end after a verb (support them financially)
entries.modifies: whole clauses, adjectives and participles, verbs
entries.form: -ly from financial; the first syllable is also said fy-
entries.contrast: Russian материально помогать is help financially, not materially — English materially means significantly (it did not materially change the result).

examples: Politically, raising taxes right before an election would be suicide.
The plan makes sense on paper, but politically it's a nonstarter.
Politically, the governor can't afford to lose the suburbs.
My grandmother was politically active her whole life.
Police say the attack was politically motivated.
It's one of the most politically divided states in the country.

senses.head: From a political point of view; when politics or public opinion is considered
examples: Politically, raising taxes right before an election would be suicide.
The plan makes sense on paper, but politically it's a nonstarter.
Politically, the governor can't afford to lose the suburbs.

senses.head: In a way connected with politics, government, or political parties
examples: My grandmother was politically active her whole life.
Police say the attack was politically motivated.
It's one of the most politically divided states in the country.

entries.type: viewpoint; also manner — in terms of politics
entries.position: any position — front with a comma as a viewpoint; before an adjective or participle (politically active)
entries.modifies: whole clauses, adjectives and participles, verbs
entries.form: -ly from political; the -al- is usually not pronounced: puh-LIT-ik-lee
entries.contrast: Politically correct is a fixed phrase: avoiding words that could offend a group, often said with irony. It does not mean correct from a political point of view. Its opposite is politically incorrect.

examples: Technically, you're still married until the judge signs the papers.
It's technically legal, but it's a terrible idea.
Technically, the store closes at nine, but they let people finish shopping.
Technically, the new phone is a big step forward.
The bridge was technically difficult to build.
She's a technically brilliant pianist, but her playing feels cold.

senses.head: According to the exact rules or the strict meaning of words, even if not in reality
examples: Technically, you're still married until the judge signs the papers.
It's technically legal, but it's a terrible idea.
Technically, the store closes at nine, but they let people finish shopping.

senses.head: In terms of technology or technique — the equipment and methods involved, or the skill shown in an art, sport, or craft
body: (технически, с технической точки зрения, в плане техники)
examples: Technically, the new phone is a big step forward.
The bridge was technically difficult to build.
She's a technically brilliant pianist, but her playing feels cold.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma for 'strictly speaking' (Technically, …); mid (it's technically legal); before an adjective (technically difficult)
entries.form: -ly from technical; the -al- is usually not pronounced: TEK-nik-lee
entries.contrast: The most common American sense has nothing to do with technology: Technically, he's still my boss means формально — the rules say so, though real life may differ, and a but often follows. Russian технически covers only sense 2. Don't confuse it with practically or virtually, which mean almost.

examples: Legally, the landlord has to return your deposit within 30 days.
Once you sign it, the contract is legally binding.
Parents are legally responsible for getting their kids to school.
You can't legally park here after 6 p.m.
You have to be 21 to buy alcohol legally.
He came into the country legally.

senses.head: From the point of view of the law; as far as the law is concerned
examples: Legally, the landlord has to return your deposit within 30 days.
Once you sign it, the contract is legally binding.
Parents are legally responsible for getting their kids to school.

senses.head: In a way that is allowed by law
examples: You can't legally park here after 6 p.m.
You have to be 21 to buy alcohol legally.
He came into the country legally.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma as a viewpoint; before an adjective (legally binding); end after a verb (buy it legally)
entries.modifies: whole clauses, adjectives and participles, verbs
entries.form: -ly from legal
entries.contrast: Legally blind is an American legal category — sight so poor (20/200 or worse with glasses) that a person qualifies for benefits — not total blindness. Where Russian says юридически, English says legally: legally binding is юридически обязывающий.

examples: Medically, there's nothing wrong with him — the pain may be stress.
Insurance only covers the surgery if it's medically necessary.
She was medically cleared to play on Saturday.
Most cases can be managed medically without an operation.
The patient was put in a medically induced coma.

senses.head: From a medical point of view; in terms of health and medicine
examples: Medically, there's nothing wrong with him — the pain may be stress.
Insurance only covers the surgery if it's medically necessary.
She was medically cleared to play on Saturday.

senses.head: By means of medical treatment, especially drugs rather than surgery
examples: Most cases can be managed medically without an operation.
The patient was put in a medically induced coma.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma as a viewpoint; before an adjective or participle (medically necessary); end after a verb (treated medically)
entries.modifies: whole clauses, adjectives and participles, verbs
entries.form: -ly from medical; the -al- is usually not pronounced: MED-ik-lee
entries.contrast: Medically is about medicine as a field; medicinally means as a medicine (herbs used medicinally). In American health insurance, medically necessary is a fixed term for the care a plan has to pay for.

examples: Personally, I think the first movie was better.
I don't care for sushi personally, but the kids love it.
Personally, I'd wait until the price drops.
The mayor personally called to apologize.
I'll deliver the check personally.
You'll be personally responsible for the equipment.
I don't know the senator personally, only from the news.
The two candidates dislike each other personally, not just politically.
Don't take it personally — he's rude to everyone.
She took the rejection very personally.

senses.head: Used to show that you are giving your own opinion
examples: Personally, I think the first movie was better.
I don't care for sushi personally, but the kids love it.
Personally, I'd wait until the price drops.

senses.head: By yourself, not through someone else
examples: The mayor personally called to apologize.
I'll deliver the check personally.
You'll be personally responsible for the equipment.

senses.head: As a person — in terms of character or a private relationship, not a professional or public role
examples: I don't know the senator personally, only from the news.
The two candidates dislike each other personally, not just politically.

senses.head: As an attack on or criticism of yourself, especially in take something personally
examples: Don't take it personally — he's rude to everyone.
She took the rejection very personally.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma for an opinion (Personally, I…); mid before the verb for 'yourself' (she personally called); end after take it or know someone
entries.comparison: not gradable — except take it very personally
entries.form: -ly from personal; double l
entries.contrast: Personally is not in person: I met him in person means face to face; I know him personally means we are acquainted, not just by name. Take it personally is the set phrase for принимать на свой счёт. The opinion sense almost always goes with I or we: Personally, I think….

examples: Theoretically, the drive takes three hours, but not with Friday traffic.
It's theoretically possible to see the northern lights from Chicago.
Theoretically, anyone can apply for the job.
The paper is theoretically interesting but has very little data.
Her research is theoretically grounded in behavioral economics.

senses.head: In theory — according to what should happen, though it may not happen in practice
examples: Theoretically, the drive takes three hours, but not with Friday traffic.
It's theoretically possible to see the northern lights from Chicago.
Theoretically, anyone can apply for the job.

senses.head: In terms of theory; from the standpoint of an academic or scientific theory
examples: The paper is theoretically interesting but has very little data.
Her research is theoretically grounded in behavioral economics.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma; mid (you could theoretically); before an adjective (it's theoretically possible)
entries.form: -ly from theoretical; the -al- is usually not pronounced
entries.contrast: Like technically, sense 1 hints that reality is different: Theoretically, it's possible usually means don't count on it. The natural partner is in practice: Theoretically…, but in practice….

examples: Statistically, flying is much safer than driving.
Statistically, most new restaurants close within a few years.
Young men are statistically more likely to get into car accidents.
The difference between the two groups was not statistically significant.
The survey results were analyzed statistically.

senses.head: According to statistics; when you look at the numbers
examples: Statistically, flying is much safer than driving.
Statistically, most new restaurants close within a few years.
Young men are statistically more likely to get into car accidents.

senses.head: By the methods of statistics
examples: The difference between the two groups was not statistically significant.
The survey results were analyzed statistically.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma as a viewpoint; before an adjective (statistically significant)
entries.form: -ly from statistical; the -al- is usually not pronounced
entries.contrast: Statistically significant is a technical term — unlikely to be the result of chance. It is not a synonym of large or important: a tiny difference can be statistically significant.

examples: Historically, this neighborhood has been home to Italian immigrants.
Mortgage rates hit historically low levels during the pandemic.
Historically, women were paid less for the same work.
The movie isn't very historically accurate.
It's a historically important building — the treaty was signed here.
Historically, the Battle of Gettysburg was the turning point of the Civil War.

senses.head: In the past, over a long period; traditionally; also compared with the past (historically low)
examples: Historically, this neighborhood has been home to Italian immigrants.
Mortgage rates hit historically low levels during the pandemic.
Historically, women were paid less for the same work.

senses.head: In terms of history; from the point of view of a historian
examples: The movie isn't very historically accurate.
It's a historically important building — the treaty was signed here.
Historically, the Battle of Gettysburg was the turning point of the Civil War.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma for 'in the past'; mid (have historically outperformed); before an adjective (historically accurate)
entries.form: -ly from both historic and historical; the -al- is usually not pronounced
entries.contrast: One adverb serves two adjectives: historic (important in history) and historical (about history), so both historically important and historically accurate. In sense 1 the tense shows whether the pattern goes on: present perfect if it still does (Historically, the state has voted Democratic), past simple if it has ended (Historically, women were paid less). In American English the article is a, not an: a historically important building.

examples: Culturally, the two countries have a lot in common.
Our school is culturally diverse — the kids speak twenty languages at home.
In some places it isn't culturally acceptable to refuse food from a host.
Culturally, Chicago has as much to offer as New York.
The town is small but culturally rich, with two theaters and a jazz club.

senses.head: In terms of a society's customs, traditions, and beliefs
body: (в культурном отношении, с точки зрения культуры)
examples: Culturally, the two countries have a lot in common.
Our school is culturally diverse — the kids speak twenty languages at home.
In some places it isn't culturally acceptable to refuse food from a host.

senses.head: In terms of the arts — music, theater, museums, and literature
examples: Culturally, Chicago has as much to offer as New York.
The town is small but culturally rich, with two theaters and a jazz club.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma; before an adjective (culturally diverse)
entries.form: -ly from cultural; double l
entries.contrast: False friend: Russian культурно (вести себя культурно) means politely, with good manners — English politely, decently. Culturally only means in terms of culture.

examples: Economically, the town never recovered after the plant closed.
The project isn't economically viable without federal money.
Kids from economically disadvantaged families get free lunch.
We're trying to live more economically until I find a new job.
Use the paint economically — it's all we have.
She writes economically, never wasting a word.

senses.head: In terms of the economy, trade, or wealth
examples: Economically, the town never recovered after the plant closed.
The project isn't economically viable without federal money.
Kids from economically disadvantaged families get free lunch.

senses.head: In a way that uses little money, time, or material, without waste
examples: We're trying to live more economically until I find a new job.
Use the paint economically — it's all we have.
She writes economically, never wasting a word.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma as a viewpoint; before an adjective (economically viable); end after a verb for 'thriftily' (live economically)
entries.comparison: more/most — only in the 'thriftily' sense (more economically); not gradable as a viewpoint
entries.modifies: whole clauses, adjectives and participles, verbs
entries.form: -ly from both economic (about the economy) and economical (saving money); also said ee-kuh-NAHM-ik-lee
entries.contrast: The two senses belong to two adjectives: economic growth (экономический) but an economical car (экономичный). The adverb is the same word, so context decides: economically weak is экономически слабый; use it economically is экономно.

entries.meaning: In terms of the practical planning and organization of people, transport, and supplies. ---
examples: Logistically, getting 200 guests to an island is a nightmare.
The move was logistically complicated, with three trucks and two dogs.
It's a great idea, but logistically we can't pull it off by June.
entries.position: any position — front with a comma; before an adjective (logistically difficult)
entries.form: -ly from logistical; the first syllable is also said loh-
entries.contrast: Not related to logic: logically is логично, по логике; logistically is about planning, transport, and supplies. Logistically impossible means it can't be organized, not that it makes no sense.

examples: The inspector said the house is structurally sound.
The bridge was structurally damaged in the earthquake.
Structurally, the old barn is in better shape than it looks.
Structurally, the novel moves between three timelines.
English and German are structurally similar.
The economy has changed structurally since the 1980s.

senses.head: In terms of how a building, bridge, or object is built and holds together
examples: The inspector said the house is structurally sound.
The bridge was structurally damaged in the earthquake.
Structurally, the old barn is in better shape than it looks.

senses.head: In terms of the way the parts of a system, text, or organization are arranged
examples: Structurally, the novel moves between three timelines.
English and German are structurally similar.
The economy has changed structurally since the 1980s.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma; before an adjective (structurally sound); end after a verb (changed structurally)
entries.form: -ly from structural; double l
entries.contrast: In engineering Russian, конструктивно (по конструкции) is structurally or in design — not constructively, which in English only means in a helpful way (constructive criticism). Structurally sound is the set phrase for a building that is safe and not about to fall down.

examples: Scientifically, there's no evidence that the diet works.
It's scientifically proven that smoking causes cancer.
The ad's claims aren't scientifically accurate.
The drug has never been scientifically tested on children.
We need to approach the problem more scientifically, one variable at a time.

senses.head: According to science; from a scientific point of view
examples: Scientifically, there's no evidence that the diet works.
It's scientifically proven that smoking causes cancer.
The ad's claims aren't scientifically accurate.

senses.head: Using the careful, systematic methods of science
examples: The drug has never been scientifically tested on children.
We need to approach the problem more scientifically, one variable at a time.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma as a viewpoint; before an adjective or participle (scientifically proven); end after a verb (test it scientifically)
entries.comparison: more/most — in the 'by scientific methods' sense (more scientifically); not gradable as a viewpoint
entries.modifies: whole clauses, adjectives and participles, verbs
entries.form: -ally from scientific (there is no scientifical); the ending is said -ik-lee

examples: Morally, what he did was wrong, even if it was legal.
I think it's morally unacceptable to lie to a patient.
Is the company morally responsible for the spill?
She tried to live morally in a business full of cheats.
Most people believe they behave more morally than their neighbors.

senses.head: From the point of view of right and wrong
examples: Morally, what he did was wrong, even if it was legal.
I think it's morally unacceptable to lie to a patient.
Is the company morally responsible for the spill?

senses.head: In a way that is right and good; by high moral standards
examples: She tried to live morally in a business full of cheats.
Most people believe they behave more morally than their neighbors.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma as a viewpoint; before an adjective (morally wrong); end after a verb (act morally)
entries.comparison: more/most — in the 'rightly' sense (more morally); not gradable as a viewpoint
entries.form: -ly from moral; double l
entries.contrast: False friend: Russian морально often means emotionally or mentally — морально тяжело is emotionally draining, морально подготовиться is prepare mentally, морально устал is mentally exhausted, and морально устаревший is outdated or obsolete. English morally is only about right and wrong; moral support is the one place the two languages match.

examples: Smoking indoors is no longer socially acceptable.
Socially, smartphones have changed how teenagers date.
The program helps socially disadvantaged kids get into college.
We work together, but we never see each other socially.
I only drink socially, maybe a beer at a barbecue.
It's hard to meet people socially after you move to a new city.
He's brilliant but socially awkward.
Our daughter did fine academically but struggled socially in middle school.

senses.head: In terms of society, social class, or what people in general accept
examples: Smoking indoors is no longer socially acceptable.
Socially, smartphones have changed how teenagers date.
The program helps socially disadvantaged kids get into college.

senses.head: In situations where people meet for pleasure, outside work or duty
body: (в компании, в неформальной обстановке, вне работы)
examples: We work together, but we never see each other socially.
I only drink socially, maybe a beer at a barbecue.
It's hard to meet people socially after you move to a new city.

senses.head: In terms of relationships with other people and the ability to get along with them
examples: He's brilliant but socially awkward.
Our daughter did fine academically but struggled socially in middle school.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma as a viewpoint; before an adjective (socially acceptable); end after a verb (see someone socially)
entries.form: -ly from social; double l
entries.contrast: I drink socially means only at parties and dinners with friends, not alone and not much — it has nothing to do with drinking in public. Don't confuse socially with sociably (in a friendly, outgoing way).

examples: After the funeral I was emotionally exhausted.
Emotionally, she's still not ready to date again.
Caring for a sick parent is emotionally draining.
He spoke emotionally about his late father.
Fans reacted emotionally when the team finally won the title.

senses.head: In terms of feelings; with regard to a person's emotional state
examples: After the funeral I was emotionally exhausted.
Emotionally, she's still not ready to date again.
Caring for a sick parent is emotionally draining.

senses.head: In a way that shows strong feelings
examples: He spoke emotionally about his late father.
Fans reacted emotionally when the team finally won the title.

entries.position: any position — before an adjective (emotionally exhausted); front with a comma as a viewpoint; end after a verb (speak emotionally)
entries.comparison: more/most — in the 'with strong feeling' sense (more emotionally); not gradable as a viewpoint
entries.modifies: adjectives and participles, whole clauses, verbs
entries.form: -ly from emotional; double l
entries.contrast: This is where Russian морально usually belongs: морально тяжело is emotionally hard or draining, моральная травма is emotional trauma. Translating it as morally turns it into a question of right and wrong.

examples: You need to be physically fit to join the fire department.
Physically, he's fine — it's his mental health we're worried about.
Construction work is physically demanding.
The company is registered in Delaware but physically located in Denver.
Students must be physically present to take the exam.
It's physically impossible to be in two places at once.
There's no way — I physically can't finish this by Friday.

senses.head: In terms of the body rather than the mind
examples: You need to be physically fit to join the fire department.
Physically, he's fine — it's his mental health we're worried about.
Construction work is physically demanding.

senses.head: In terms of material things or actual presence, as opposed to online, on paper, or in the mind
examples: The company is registered in Delaware but physically located in Denver.
Students must be physically present to take the exam.

senses.head: According to the laws of nature; in reality at all
examples: It's physically impossible to be in two places at once.
There's no way — I physically can't finish this by Friday.

entries.position: any position — before an adjective (physically fit); front with a comma as a viewpoint; mid before a verb (physically attacked)
entries.modifies: adjectives and participles, whole clauses, verbs
entries.form: -ly from physical; the -al- is usually not pronounced: FIZ-ik-lee
entries.contrast: In everyday English physically is about the body or the material world; for the school subject say in terms of physics. In casual American speech I physically can't is an exaggeration for I really can't.

examples: Marathon runners have to be mentally tough.
He was mentally ill for years before anyone noticed.
Mentally, I'm ready for the exam; I just need some sleep.
I mentally added up the bill while the waiter talked.
She mentally went over her speech one more time.

senses.head: In terms of the mind or mental health
examples: Marathon runners have to be mentally tough.
He was mentally ill for years before anyone noticed.
Mentally, I'm ready for the exam; I just need some sleep.

senses.head: In your mind, without speaking, writing, or doing anything
examples: I mentally added up the bill while the waiter talked.
She mentally went over her speech one more time.

entries.position: any position — before an adjective (mentally ill); front with a comma as a viewpoint; mid before a verb for 'in your head' (mentally calculated)
entries.modifies: adjectives and participles, whole clauses, verbs
entries.form: -ly from mental; double l
entries.contrast: Russian морально готов and морально устал are mentally ready and mentally exhausted, not morally. Avoid mentally retarded: it is now offensive; American English says intellectual disability.

examples: The new bridge officially opens on Monday.
The White House has not officially confirmed the report.
You aren't officially enrolled until you pay the fee.
Officially, he resigned; everyone knows he was fired.
Officially, the trip was about trade, but the senator spent most of it on the beach.
It's ninety degrees — summer is officially here.
I'm officially addicted to this show.

senses.head: By people in authority or according to the rules; for the record
examples: The new bridge officially opens on Monday.
The White House has not officially confirmed the report.
You aren't officially enrolled until you pay the fee.

senses.head: According to what is said publicly, which may not be the whole truth
examples: Officially, he resigned; everyone knows he was fired.
Officially, the trip was about trade, but the senator spent most of it on the beach.

senses.head: Informal: now definitely, beyond any doubt
examples: It's ninety degrees — summer is officially here.
I'm officially addicted to this show.

entries.position: any position — mid before the verb (officially opens); front with a comma for the public version (Officially, …)
entries.modifies: verbs, whole clauses, adjectives and participles
entries.form: -ly from official; double l
entries.contrast: Russian официально also means formal in style — официально одет is formally dressed, официальный тон is a formal tone. English officially only means by authority or for the record. Sense 3 (It's officially summer) is informal but very common in American speech.

examples: Ideally, we'd leave by six to beat the traffic.
Ideally, the new hire would speak Spanish.
You should ideally get seven to eight hours of sleep.
The hotel is ideally located, two blocks from the beach.
With all that patience, she's ideally suited to teaching.

senses.head: In the best possible situation; if things were exactly as you want them
examples: Ideally, we'd leave by six to beat the traffic.
Ideally, the new hire would speak Spanish.
You should ideally get seven to eight hours of sleep.

senses.head: Perfectly; in the best possible way, used with a few participles
examples: The hotel is ideally located, two blocks from the beach.
With all that patience, she's ideally suited to teaching.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma for 'in an ideal world' (Ideally, …); mid (you should ideally); before a participle for 'perfectly' (ideally located)
entries.form: -ly from ideal; double l
entries.contrast: Russian идеально is usually perfectly: идеально убрано is perfectly clean, всё прошло идеально is everything went perfectly. English ideally in that sense goes only with a few participles — suited, located, placed, positioned, situated. Otherwise ideally means in an ideal world.

examples: Ethically, a therapist can't date a patient.
Paying people for five-star reviews is ethically questionable.
The study raises ethically difficult questions about privacy.
We only buy ethically sourced coffee.
Companies are under pressure to behave more ethically.

senses.head: From the point of view of moral rules, especially the rules of a profession
examples: Ethically, a therapist can't date a patient.
Paying people for five-star reviews is ethically questionable.
The study raises ethically difficult questions about privacy.

senses.head: In a morally correct and fair way
examples: We only buy ethically sourced coffee.
Companies are under pressure to behave more ethically.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma as a viewpoint; before an adjective or participle (ethically sourced); end after a verb (act ethically)
entries.comparison: more/most — in the 'fairly and honestly' sense (more ethically); not gradable as a viewpoint
entries.modifies: whole clauses, adjectives and participles, verbs
entries.form: -ly from ethical; the -al- is usually not pronounced: ETH-ik-lee
entries.contrast: Russian splits этически (from the point of view of ethics) and этично (in an ethical way); English uses ethically for both. Ethically is the usual word for professional rules — medicine, law, business, journalism — where morally would sound personal or religious.

entries.meaning: In terms of location, distance, or the physical features of an area. ---
examples: Geographically, Alaska is closer to Russia than to the rest of the United States.
The two towns are geographically close but very different culturally.
Our sales team is geographically spread out across four time zones.
entries.position: any position — front with a comma; before an adjective (geographically close)
entries.form: -ly from geographical or geographic; the -al- is usually not pronounced

examples: Biologically, whales are mammals, not fish.
Teenagers are biologically wired to stay up late.
Some of these chemicals stay biologically active for years.
We're not biologically related — my dad married her mom.
He raised the boy, though he wasn't biologically his father.

senses.head: In terms of biology; from the point of view of how living things work
examples: Biologically, whales are mammals, not fish.
Teenagers are biologically wired to stay up late.
Some of these chemicals stay biologically active for years.

senses.head: By birth; in terms of genes rather than adoption or marriage
examples: We're not biologically related — my dad married her mom.
He raised the boy, though he wasn't biologically his father.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma; before an adjective (biologically related)
entries.form: -ly from biological; the -al- is usually not pronounced
entries.contrast: Russian био- on food labels (биопродукты) is organic in English, not biologically grown. Sense 2 is the everyday American use in family talk: biologically related, as opposed to adopted or step-.

examples: The film was loved by critics but failed commercially.
Commercially, it was the band's biggest album.
It's a great invention, but is it commercially viable?
The vaccine won't be commercially available until next year.
Most commercially grown tomatoes are picked before they're ripe.

senses.head: In terms of making money; as a business
examples: The film was loved by critics but failed commercially.
Commercially, it was the band's biggest album.
It's a great invention, but is it commercially viable?

senses.head: Made, grown, or offered for sale to the public, rather than privately or for research
examples: The vaccine won't be commercially available until next year.
Most commercially grown tomatoes are picked before they're ripe.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma as a viewpoint; before an adjective or participle (commercially available); end after a verb (failed commercially)
entries.modifies: whole clauses, adjectives and participles, verbs
entries.form: -ly from commercial; double l
entries.contrast: Commercially available means anyone can buy it in stores or online — not that it is expensive, advertised, or sold by a private company. Russian коммерческий in the sense of paid or private (коммерческий вуз) is private or for-profit, not commercial.

examples: Paper straws are more environmentally friendly than plastic ones.
Environmentally, the new pipeline is a disaster waiting to happen.
The wetlands are environmentally sensitive, so building there is restricted.
Doctors don't know whether the disease is inherited or environmentally caused.
Some asthma attacks are environmentally triggered.

senses.head: In terms of the natural world and its protection
examples: Paper straws are more environmentally friendly than plastic ones.
Environmentally, the new pipeline is a disaster waiting to happen.
The wetlands are environmentally sensitive, so building there is restricted.

senses.head: Caused by surroundings and living conditions rather than by genes
examples: Doctors don't know whether the disease is inherited or environmentally caused.
Some asthma attacks are environmentally triggered.

entries.position: any position — before an adjective (environmentally friendly); front with a comma
entries.form: -ly from environmental; double l
entries.contrast: Russian экологически чистый is environmentally friendly for a product and clean or organic for food or a place; плохая экология is pollution, not bad ecology. In everyday American English environmentally is far more common than ecologically, which sounds scientific.

examples: Visually, the movie is stunning, but the story is thin.
The new website is much more visually appealing.
The two apps are visually almost identical.
The mechanic checked the brakes visually before the test drive.
The software helps visually impaired students read their textbooks.

senses.head: In terms of how something looks
examples: Visually, the movie is stunning, but the story is thin.
The new website is much more visually appealing.
The two apps are visually almost identical.

senses.head: By looking, or in terms of the ability to see
examples: The mechanic checked the brakes visually before the test drive.
The software helps visually impaired students read their textbooks.

entries.position: any position — front with a comma as a viewpoint; before an adjective (visually stunning); end after a verb (inspected visually)
entries.modifies: whole clauses, adjectives and participles, verbs
entries.form: -ly from visual; double l
entries.contrast: Russian визуально is often everyday speech for by the look of it — визуально всё в порядке is it looks fine, and знать визуально is know by sight. English visually is more formal and technical. Visually impaired is the polite American term for people who are blind or partly blind.
